items.title: Apple Still Working on Giant Foldable iPad That Could Cost $5,000
items.summary: Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman . Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "…
items.body: Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman . Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "Project J312." He described it as a foldable iPad with a display measuring around 19 to 20 inches, saying it would resemble a "gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside." The device could cost between $3,000 and $5,000. Apple apparently originally wanted to announce the device by 2027, before pushing that target to 2028. The timeframe has since slipped to around 2029, although Gurman cautioned that it remains uncertain whether the product will ever reach the market. Gurman cited cost and display manufacturing yield issues among the obstacles facing development, along with concerns that the ‌iPad‌ could be cumbersome. Apple has also yet to determine which operating system it would run, with macOS, iPadOS, and an entirely new platform all remaining possibilities. Gurman described the unresolved software direction as another complication, but expressed excitement about the device's potential. The comments follow a report from research firm Omdia in September, which claimed that Apple had canceled plans for a foldable MacBook measuring between 16.1 and 18 inches when unfolded. Earlier reports had described that device as a large-screened foldable ‌iPad‌, although it remains unclear whether Omdia was referring to the same project Gurman discussed. Gurman discussed the foldable ‌iPad‌ in April, describing it as a priority for John Ternus while warning that it could remain an unreleased experiment. The potential 2029 timeframe was already part of Gurman's report from October 2025 , when weight and display technology issues were said to threaten Apple's earlier 2028 target. items.summary: The platform is also testing a repositioned Google Maps speedometer, while adding more OEM icons.

Android Auto is working on a new Details page for easier bug reporting

The platform is also testing a repositioned Google Maps speedometer, while adding more OEM icons.

•

Andy Walker / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

TL;DR

• Android Auto is working on a new Details page in settings that provides all the relevant information about a device and display.

• There’s also a button to copy all the vehicle and device information, which should make it easier to report bugs.

• We also found a relocated speedometer in Google Maps, plus a bunch of new manufacturer icons that could land in a future update.

Android Auto is no stranger to bugs, and a future version of the app could make it easier to submit your device/car information in bug reports. Google is working on an updated Connected vehicles page with a new option to instantly copy and share relevant details.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

We examined Android Auto version 18.3.164844 to enable a new Details option from the Android Auto settings page. This opens a “Vehicle information” dialog containing all the necessary information, including the car’s make and model, software version, display dimensions, and more.

As you would expect, the display details in the Vehicle information dialog are visible only when you’re connected to Android Auto. Meanwhile, there’s a Copy option here that lets you paste all these details into a bug report instantly.

When available, this new Details option should appear on the Connected vehicles page, accessible by tapping Vehicles in Android Auto settings, then tapping your car’s name. Currently, this page only contains the Forget and Rename options.

While we managed to uncover visuals of the new Details page in Android Auto settings, a string in the app’s code reveals another future addition.

Code

<string name="locked_app_not_supported_toast">This app is locked and cannot be opened in Android Auto</string>

Users will likely see the above toast when trying to open an Android Auto-compatible app that’s been locked via the upcoming app lock functionality. While app lock isn’t widely available on Android just yet, this string suggests Google is laying the groundwork for its future arrival.

Additionally, the Google Maps experience in Android Auto could get a minor tweak, with the speedometer icon moving from the bottom-left of the screen to the top-left. This opens up space in the bottom-left portion of the screen, which can sometimes be blocked by the speedometer.

Lastly, Android Auto is in the process of adding new OEM icons to the system. We’re seeing a handful of popular OEMs here, including some motorcycle brands.

The icon typically appears as the first option in the app drawer, as shown in the second screenshot above. Tapping this icon lets users exit the Android Auto experience instantly.

Since we had to manually activate some of these features, it’s hard to say when Android Auto will incorporate these changes. All we can do is hope that it happens sooner rather than later.

items.body:
iPhones Dominate China's Weak Singles' Day Smartphone Sales

Thursday November 26, 2026 4:55 am PST by Tim Hardwick

Apple held the top spot in China's smartphone market during the country's Singles' Day shopping festival, despite an 8% year-over-year sales decline, according to Counterpoint Research. The overall market fell 17% across the promotional period, defined as weeks 42–46.

Six of the top 10 bestsellers were iPhone 17 and 18 models, led by the iPhone 18 Pro Max, with the iPhone Duo at No. 9. Huawei was the only major brand to grow in the period, rising by 29%. Counterpoint says buyers are postponing upgrades rather than accepting higher prices, following strong iPhone 18 Pro sales in China at launch.

items.summary: Like other apps, YouTube limits custom icons to Premium subscribers.
items.body:

Mobile

You can now change YouTube’s app icon on your phone, but only if you pay for it

Like other apps, YouTube limits custom icons to Premium subscribers.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 7:32 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• YouTube is now letting Premium subscribers change its app icon.

• The current selection includes three options for the icon.

• YouTube has been testing seven app icons in total, but four are missing from the current rollout.

Several prominent apps, including X, Telegram, Reddit, and Instagram, let users swap out the default app icon for something else. Often, this perk is available only to users who pay for the experience. Last month, we learned that YouTube is also working on a similar feature that lets Premium subscribers change the app icon, and it already appears to be rolling out for some folks.

User Radu Oncescu on X posted screenshots of the setting that lets users change the default icon to one of the three other options currently available. These include one with a shiny, metal-like finish, somewhat like a silver YouTube Play button, another one featuring what look like brush strokes using red paint, and a third one with a pixel effect and a gradient over the icon.

X / Radu Oncescu

These options appear under Settings > General > Premium app icon inside the YouTube app. While we spotted the feature being tested on Android, the user notes that it’s available on iOS. Another report from user howfxr on X last week suggests the feature also cropped up for some Android users.

X / howfxr

In both cases, the rollout does not seem to be widespread, and we don’t have it on any of our devices yet. So we recommend not fretting if you don’t have it either yet. It’s not like YouTube is bringing back the original logo with the name spelled out anyway.

Meanwhile, YouTube has been testing four more icon options, including some retro ones, but none appear to be available for now. We’ll keep an eye out for when those might be available.

Google is working on gamepad profiles for Android’s controller remapping feature

You might not have to remap your controller every time you launch a different game.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 7:12 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google is working on adding support for multiple gamepad profiles in Android.

• Code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 hints at a new interface for managing gamepad profiles.

• The feature could let users switch between gamepad button layouts on the fly.

If you’re a mobile gamer, you probably use controllers for many Android games. Customizing a controller’s layout can be quite useful, especially if you like using different layouts for different games. Although Google added support for game controller remapping with Android 17, it currently lets you keep only one layout saved at a time. Fortunately, Google is now working to improve the feature with support for multiple gamepad profiles.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

While digging through the code in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4, we spotted several strings that point to an upcoming gamepad profile management interface. According to the strings, there could be a “Default” profile, along with options to edit and delete individual profiles. We also spotted strings hinting at a “More options” menu for each profile.

Here are the strings we found related to the feature:

Code

<string name="gamepad_profile_default_title">Default</string>
<string name="gamepad_profile_menu_delete">Delete</string>
<string name="gamepad_profile_menu_edit">Edit</string>
<string name="gamepad_profile_more_options_content_description">More options for %1$s</string>

We also gathered some details on how the feature will work by taking a closer look at the code. Android will distinguish between “default” and “global” profiles, and it seems the global profiles will be reusable across controllers. We also spotted functionality to retrieve saved profiles, switch between them, and identify the active profile. Android could also let users edit the default profile, but won’t let them delete it.

Here are the references we spotted in the code:

Code

default_profile
global_profile_
getGamepadProfileHeaders
getAppliedGamepadProfiles
applyGamepadProfile
deleteGamepadProfile
launchEditProfileFragment

Letting gamers create multiple gamepad profiles could let them set up custom button layouts for different game styles. Instead of manually remapping buttons every time, the feature could let you simply switch between saved profiles.

The feature isn’t live yet, and we couldn’t get it to show up on our test device. However, since we’re already seeing the groundwork for a dedicated gamepad layout interface, it seems Google is making progress on the feature.

items.summary: Don’t pay full price for your next flagship. Here’s when Samsung, Google and Apple phones get their biggest discounts.

Mobile

These are the best times to buy a new phone if you want to save money

Don’t pay full price for your next flagship. Here’s when Samsung, Google and Apple phones get their biggest discounts.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 7:00 AM ET

•

•

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

Buying a flagship phone on launch day without a good trade-in deal is one of the easiest ways to overspend in 2026. Smartphone prices are shooting northwards, largely because of growing demand for AI components in data centers and constrained supply for practically everything else, including smartphones.

You’d be surprised to learn that memory costs have gone from accounting for 13% of a phone’s total component costs in early 2025 to more than 40% by late 2026. As a result, major brands have passed those costs on to buyers. Flagships like the Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro now start $100 higher than their predecessors and spending well over $1,000 on a new phone is becoming the norm.

Smartphone prices have never been higher, but knowing when to buy can save you hundreds of dollars.

But, let’s be real, nobody wants to or should have to pay full price on a smartphone. Smartphone prices change throughout the year, and buying at the right time can save you hundreds of dollars. Whether you’re considering the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra or Apple’s latest Pro model, there are three key buying windows worth watching in the US. And as we head into, arguably, the biggest time of the year to save big on your smartphone purchase, knowing when to shop can make a big difference to your budget.

Readers' poll

When do you usually buy a new flagship phone?

0 votes

Pre-order periods can offer everything from storage upgrades to gift cards

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Generally speaking, the period between the announcement of the phone and before it goes on sale is one of the better times to upgrade if you’re convinced that you want the latest and greatest. Manufacturers use this period to attract early buyers with generous promotions instead of direct discounts. If you have a recent flagship to trade in, pre-ordering can be a particularly good deal and get you significant discounts, trade-in benefits and freebies.

Pre-order deals can save you money upfront. However, free storage upgrades, gift cards and trade-in bonuses can make them worthwhile too.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is a good example. During its pre-order period earlier this year, retailers like Best Buy and Amazon offered a free storage upgrade and, in some cases, additional benefits. That meant buyers could get the 512GB model for the price of the 256GB version, along with some extra money to spend on accessories. Amazon even tossed in a $200 gift card alongside a discount 0n the Buds 4 Pro saving you as much as $437.50. That’s a solid chunk of change.

Google took a similar approach with the Pixel 11 Pro, offering $200 in store credit to offset its higher $1,099 starting price. Apple, meanwhile, relies more heavily on carrier promotions. Buyers who pre-ordered the iPhone 18 Pro through AT&T or Verizon could get up to $1,200 in bill credits with an eligible trade-in. These deals could cover the full cost of the phone, although they required a 36-month installment plan. There are always some conditions attached to pre-order benefits, like requiring a new line, or eligible trade-ins, but the fact of the matter is that if you’re willing to shop around, there are a lot of opportunities to save.

Prime Day is a good opportunity for a major discount

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

If you miss the pre-order deals or prefer buying an unlocked phone without signing up for a carrier plan, Amazon’s Prime Day sales events are the next big sales period worth watching. Unlike previous years, Amazon now holds two major Prime Day shopping events each year. Prime Day takes place around the end of June or early July, while Prime Big Deal Days arrives in October and both events bring straight-up discounts on phones. This means you don’t need a trade-in or a long-term carrier agreement to save money. It’s the smarter move in my books.

If you want an unlocked Android flagship without committing to a carrier, Prime Day discounts are a great opportunity.

Android flagships also tend to lose value fairly quickly compared to their Apple counterpart, and Prime Day is often when those price drops become more noticeable. We saw this with the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra and Google Pixel 10 in 2025. Both phones received discounts ranging between 20% and 30% across Prime Day events. That’s significant.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra followed a similar pattern this year. During this summer’s Prime Day sale, its unlocked price dropped by $380 to $920. That’s a 29% discount just a few months after launch. Sticking to the timeline, the October Prime Day sale brought an even steeper $420 discount on the Galaxy S26 Ultra. If you want a high-end Android phone without committing to carrier installments, waiting until summer or later invariably pays off.

While the latest iPhones don’t usually get a steep discount on Prime Day, you can usually expect freebies like a pair of AirPods, discounts on older generations of iPhones.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday bring the steepest discounts

Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority

Early Black Friday deals are already live across major US retailers and carriers, giving us a good indication of the discounts to expect for Black Friday this year. Additionally, looking at the data for previous years, it is safe to say that late November is one of the best times to buy a flagship. Brands tend to offer some of their biggest discounts of the year to attract holiday shoppers, especially those looking for unlocked phones.

Black Friday is the last big sales period of the year, and is also when you can snag the best deals on the latest phones.

Google, in particular, is known for its aggressive Black Friday discounts, and this year is no different. The unlocked Pixel 11 Pro has already dropped to an all-time low of $749 on Amazon. That’s $350, or 32%, off its original $1,099 price. The Google Store is also offering up to $400 off the Pixel 11 Pro lineup, along with higher trade-in values. That’s a great start if you’ve been eyeing a Pixel 11 Pro for less.

Samsung is offering similar savings. Its online store has knocked $350 off the Galaxy S26 Ultra, with an additional $100 PayPal promo code bringing the price down to $949.99. Buyers also get $150 in accessory credit. It goes without saying that you can save a lot more if you are open to considering older, but still very good smartphones.

Like with other sales events, options for Apple buyers tend to be a bit limited. Right now, the biggest savings I could find were with carriers like T-Mobile that are offering 36-month trade-in credits. Meanwhile, Best Buy is offering just a $100 discount on an unlocked iPhone 17 Pro.

The iPhone 18 Pro is following a similar pattern. Apple usually runs a gift card promotion starting Black Friday through to Cyber Monday giving you anywhere from a $25 to $300 gift coupon depending on the product you’re purchasing. The iPhone 18 Pro, however, is excluded from this promo which means the best savings you’ll get will be from carriers.

The right buying window can save you hundreds on your next flagship

Ultimately, getting a good deal on a flagship in 2026 comes down to knowing when and how to buy and these sales periods aren’t hard to predict. Unless you’re absolutely convinced by your choice of upgrade, or are looking at picking up a new iPhone, pre-order discounts aren’t usually the best bet. If you’re eyeing an unlocked Android phone without committing to a carrier plan, waiting for Prime Day, or Black Friday is invariably the smarter move as it can save you hundreds of dollars.

Flagships like the Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Google Pixel 11 Pro now start $100 higher than their predecessors and spending well over $1,000 on a new phone is becoming the norm.
Smartphone prices have never been higher, but knowing when to buy can save you hundreds of dollars.

But, let’s be real, nobody wants to or should have to pay full price on a smartphone. Smartphone prices change throughout the year, and buying at the right time can save you hundreds of dollars. Whether you’re considering the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra or Apple’s latest Pro model, there are three key buying windows worth watching in the US. And as we head into, arguably, the biggest time of the year to save big on your smartphone purchase, knowing when to shop can make a big difference to your budget.

When do you usually buy a new flagship phone?

Pre-order periods can offer everything from storage upgrades to gift cards

blocks.alt: Pixel 11 Pro laying on a white pillow.

blocks.text: Joe Maring / Android Authority

Generally speaking, the period between the announcement of the phone and before it goes on sale is one of the better times to upgrade if you’re convinced that you want the latest and greatest. Manufacturers use this period to attract early buyers with generous promotions instead of direct discounts. If you have a recent flagship to trade in, pre-ordering can be a particularly good deal and get you significant discounts, trade-in benefits and freebies.
Pre-order deals can save you money upfront. However, free storage upgrades, gift cards and trade-in bonuses can make them worthwhile too.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is a good example. During its pre-order period earlier this year, retailers like Best Buy and Amazon offered a free storage upgrade and, in some cases, additional benefits. That meant buyers could get the 512GB model for the price of the 256GB version, along with some extra money to spend on accessories. Amazon even tossed in a $200 gift card alongside a discount 0n the Buds 4 Pro saving you as much as $437.50. That’s a solid chunk of change.

Google took a similar approach with the Pixel 11 Pro, offering $200 in store credit to offset its higher $1,099 starting price. Apple, meanwhile, relies more heavily on carrier promotions. Buyers who pre-ordered the iPhone 18 Pro through AT&T or Verizon could get up to $1,200 in bill credits with an eligible trade-in. These deals could cover the full cost of the phone, although they required a 36-month installment plan. There are always some conditions attached to pre-order benefits, like requiring a new line, or eligible trade-ins, but the fact of the matter is that if you’re willing to shop around, there are a lot of opportunities to save.
Prime Day is a good opportunity for a major discount

blocks.alt: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra with S Pen out in hand

blocks.text: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

If you miss the pre-order deals or prefer buying an unlocked phone without signing up for a carrier plan, Amazon’s Prime Day sales events are the next big sales period worth watching. Unlike previous years, Amazon now holds two major Prime Day shopping events each year. Prime Day takes place around the end of June or early July, while Prime Big Deal Days arrives in October and both events bring straight-up discounts on phones. This means you don’t need a trade-in or a long-term carrier agreement to save money. It’s the smarter move in my books.
If you want an unlocked Android flagship without committing to a carrier, Prime Day discounts are a great opportunity.

Android flagships also tend to lose value fairly quickly compared to their Apple counterpart, and Prime Day is often when those price drops become more noticeable. We saw this with the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra and Google Pixel 10 in 2025. Both phones received discounts ranging between 20% and 30% across Prime Day events. That’s significant.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra followed a similar pattern this year. During this summer’s Prime Day sale, its unlocked price dropped by $380 to $920. That’s a 29% discount just a few months after launch. Sticking to the timeline, the October Prime Day sale brought an even steeper $420 discount on the Galaxy S26 Ultra. If you want a high-end Android phone without committing to carrier installments, waiting until summer or later invariably pays off.
While the latest iPhones don’t usually get a steep discount on Prime Day, you can usually expect freebies like a pair of AirPods, discounts on older generations of iPhones.
Black Friday and Cyber Monday bring the steepest discounts
Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority

Early Black Friday deals are already live across major US retailers and carriers, giving us a good indication of the discounts to expect for Black Friday this year. Additionally, looking at the data for previous years, it is safe to say that late November is one of the best times to buy a flagship. Brands tend to offer some of their biggest discounts of the year to attract holiday shoppers, especially those looking for unlocked phones.
Black Friday is the last big sales period of the year, and is also when you can snag the best deals on the latest phones.

Google, in particular, is known for its aggressive Black Friday discounts, and this year is no different. The unlocked Pixel 11 Pro has already dropped to an all-time low of $749 on Amazon. That’s $350, or 32%, off its original $1,099 price. The Google Store is also offering up to $400 off the Pixel 11 Pro lineup, along with higher trade-in values. That’s a great start if you’ve been eyeing a Pixel 11 Pro for less.

Samsung is offering similar savings. Its online store has knocked $350 off the Galaxy S26 Ultra, with an additional $100 PayPal promo code bringing the price down to $949.99. Buyers also get $150 in accessory credit. It goes without saying that you can save a lot more if you are open to considering older, but still very good smartphones.

Like with other sales events, options for Apple buyers tend to be a bit limited. Right now, the biggest savings I could find were with carriers like T-Mobile that are offering 36-month trade-in credits. Meanwhile, Best Buy is offering just a $100 discount on an unlocked iPhone 17 Pro.

The iPhone 18 Pro is following a similar pattern. Apple usually runs a gift card promotion starting Black Friday through to Cyber Monday giving you anywhere from a $25 to $300 gift coupon depending on the product you’re purchasing. The iPhone 18 Pro, however, is excluded from this promo which means the best savings you’ll get will be from carriers.
The right buying window can save you hundreds on your next flagship

Ultimately, getting a good deal on a flagship in 2026 comes down to knowing when and how to buy and these sales periods aren’t hard to predict. Unless you’re absolutely convinced by your choice of upgrade, or are looking at picking up a new iPhone, pre-order discounts aren’t usually the best bet. If you’re eyeing an unlocked Android phone without committing to a carrier plan, waiting for Prime Day, or Black Friday is invariably the smarter move as it can save you hundreds of dollars.

Samsung’s Recompose tool could let you shift a photo’s perspective with AI in One UI 9.5

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals a Photo Assist tool that could convert still shots into 3D scenes to change camera angles.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 6:48 AM ET

•

•

Robert Triggs / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 suggests Samsung is working on Recompose, a Galaxy AI tool in Photo Assist that could let you change a photo’s angle and perspective after you’ve taken it.

• Recompose appears to build a 3D version of your photo on-device using Samsung’s Spatial Core add-on, before Samsung’s cloud generates the final image.

• Recompose is hidden on the Galaxy S26 Ultra for now, and the same code shows Photo Assist’s Style tool switching to a new image model labeled “GPT”.

Samsung has been steadily turning its Gallery app into a Galaxy AI photo editor. Photo Assist can already erase objects, move and resize them, expand backgrounds, restyle your shots, and edit them with text prompts. With One UI 9.5, Samsung also added a Live effect tool that turns still photos into 3D wallpapers. Now, code in the One UI 9.5 beta suggests the two ideas are coming together. Samsung appears to be working on a tool called Recompose, which could let you change the angle of a photo after you’ve taken it.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Recompose could let you change the angle of your photos

We found Recompose inside Samsung’s Photo Editor app in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on our Galaxy S26 Ultra. It sits within Photo Assist’s Move tool, which currently only lets you straighten a photo on the S26 Ultra. On supported devices, the Move tool could gain a switch button to toggle between “Move” and “Recompose”, along with a reset button.

Code

<string name="move_genai">Move</string>
<string name="recompose_toggle_segment">Recompose</string>
<string name="reset_recompose">Reset</string>

According to the strings in the app, users would be able to drag the photo with one finger to change its perspective, and use two fingers to pan, zoom, and rotate it. A dolly-zoom slider would let you push the background closer or farther away, like the classic camera trick used in films.

Code

<string name="drag_one_finger_change_perspective">Drag with one finger to change the perspective. Use two fingers to pan, zoom, and rotate.</string>
<string name="dolly_zoom_tip_body">Move this slider to make background objects appear closer or farther away.</string>

Samsung’s settings description for the feature also sees some changes. On phones that support Recompose, Photo Assist’s eraser and move settings promise you can “change the angle and perspective of your photos.”

Code

<string name="eraser_and_move_setting_detail">Erase or move people and objects, expand backgrounds, or change the angle and perspective of your photos.</string>

On our S26 Ultra, the description sticks to erasing, moving, and resizing.

Code

<string name="eraser_and_move_setting_detail_not_support_recompose">Erase, move, and resize people and objects, then use AI to fill in the background.</string>

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Samsung’s Gallery app also has a few Recompose changes of its own. On supported devices, Photo Assist’s settings appear to be split into “AI eraser” and “Adjust”, with Recompose, Perspective, Move, and Fill background listed as search keywords for the latter.

Code

<string name="recompose">Recompose</string>
<string name="perspective">Perspective</string>
<string name="adjust">Adjust</string>
<string name="ai_eraser">AI eraser</string>
<string name="fill_background">Fill background</string>

Recompose appears to build a 3D model of your photo on your phone

Based on the app code, Recompose seems to work in two stages. First, Photo Editor would ask a separate Spatial Core app to turn your photo into a 3D scene with a depth map, using the photo’s focal length and a mask of the main subject. Users would then be able to change the perspective in a 3D view. Finally, Photo Editor will send the original image and the new angle to Samsung’s cloud, which would generate the finished photo.

What is Spatial Core, you ask? Spatial Core is the same 153MB Galaxy Store add-on that One UI 9.5’s Live effect asks you to download.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Photo Editor will check for Spatial Core before it opens Recompose, the same way Live effect does, and both download the same add-on app. Spatial Core includes the 3D scene function Recompose calls, and most of its size appears to be ArcSoft’s 3D photo models. The app doesn’t request internet access, so the 3D step appears geared to run entirely on your phone.

The generative fill, on the other hand, always goes to the cloud. Unlike Samsung’s other Photo Assist edits, there’s no on-device option for this step in the code. So, like Samsung’s other generative edits, Recompose will likely need an internet connection and a Samsung account.

Samsung also appears to be testing which model handles the fill. A hidden internal setting labeled “3D recomposition Model” offers two options, “NB2” and “NB2.1”. These seem to refer to Google’s Nano Banana 2 and 2.1 image models, though the setting is removed from the app’s settings page in this build.

Not every photo will work with Recompose

It looks like Recompose could come with a few limits. Based on the code, the shorter edge of your photo likely needs to be at least 500 pixels, and the aspect ratio has to fall between 9:21 and 21:9. Larger photos will likely be scaled down to 12MP before processing.

Code

<string name="cant_recompose_image_too_small">Can't recompose image because it's too small.</string>
<string name="cant_recompose_image_too_wide_or_tall">Can't recompose image because it's too wide or tall.</string>

Recompose doesn’t work on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet

Even with Spatial Core installed, Recompose remained hidden on our S26 Ultra during our testing. We only see the “Move” option in photos, but no “Recompose.”

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

The S26 Ultra meets the feature’s 3D photo requirement, but Samsung has also tied Recompose to a newer Galaxy AI version than our Galaxy S26 Ultra currently reports. It’s not clear yet whether Samsung will raise that version for the S26 series in a later update or keep Recompose for newer devices.

Photo Assist’s Style tool could switch to a model called “GPT”

Recompose isn’t the only Photo Assist change behind the same Galaxy AI version gate. Photo Assist’s Style tool, which turns your photos into styles like oil paintings and is called Restyle in the code, appears to be getting a new image model.

Photo Editor’s code lists four model versions for the tool: IMAGEN_2, IMAGEN_3, GEMPIX, and a new GPT.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

On our S26 Ultra, Photo Editor asks Samsung’s servers for GEMPIX, which matches the codename Google has used for its Nano Banana image models. On devices with the newer Galaxy AI version, Photo Editor switches to GPT.

Given the naming, “GPT” could point to one of OpenAI’s image models. However, nothing on the Style tool’s request path ties it to OpenAI: the phone only sends the version label to Samsung’s servers. Samsung’s servers then decide which model actually runs, so “GPT” could just as easily be an internal label. Samsung and OpenAI already have a working relationship: Samsung supplies OpenAI with chips and has rolled out ChatGPT Enterprise to its employees. However, neither company has announced an image model deal for Galaxy AI.

Samsung hasn’t officially announced Recompose or the new image model for the Style tool. We’ll keep you updated when we learn more.

HONOR could be cooking up a phone with three 200MP cameras

Though it's unreasonable to expect it soon.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 6:48 AM ET

•

•

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• HONOR is reportedly working on a phone with three 200MP cameras.

• The phone is rumored to feature a 1/1.5-inch sensor for the 200MP ultrawide-angle camera.

• While it’s likely to be the Magic 10 Pro Max, it cannot be confirmed just yet.

HONOR is among the phone brands already on the bandwagon for 200MP cameras on its phones. In fact, its latest flagship, the Magic 9 Pro Max, features not one but two 200MP cameras. And it looks like HONOR will move even further with a yet-to-launch phone, furnishing it with three 200MP cameras.

Leaker Digital Chat Station recently claimed in a Weibo post that HONOR is looking to use three 200MP cameras on an upcoming phone. Without mentioning the phone’s name or series, the leaker adds that the third camera, i.e., the ultrawide, will also utilize a 200MP sensor with a 1/1.5-inch format.

Digital Chat Station

The HONOR Magic 9 Pro Max, which launched outside of China earlier this week, comes with a 200MP primary and a 200MP telephoto. Meanwhile, the ultrawide uses a 1/2.88-inch 50MP sensor. So, if the leak is accurate, HONOR could move to a much bigger sensor for the ultrawide lens as well, expanding room for low-light photography and cropping.

If the phone is indeed from the Magic 10 series (or the successor to the Magic 9 series but with a different name), we could only expect it to arrive later in 2027. The only existing phone with three 200MP cameras is the OPPO Find X10 Pro Max, but it’s fair to expect more such phones to crop up by then. The Magic 10 series is also expected to introduce support for LOFIC, which is currently missing on the Magic 9 Pro Max. Other leaks about the Magic 10 series point to it featuring a variable aperture and using a Tandem OLED display.

Kindle Colorsoft gets $120 off for Black Friday, its best price

Amazon's color e-reader is 41% off, putting comics, cookbooks, and book covers in full color for less.

•

Color changes what an e-reader can do, from comic panels to cookbook photos, and Amazon’s Kindle Colorsoft brings it without giving up the easy-on-the-eyes E Ink screen Kindles are known for. It’s $169.99 on Amazon, down from its $289.99 list price. That’s $120 off, a 41% discount, and it matches the lowest price it has ever sold for.

The 7-inch display shows text at 300 ppi in black and white and 150 ppi in color, so book covers, illustrations, and charts come to life in a way a black-and-white Kindle can’t match. Because it’s E Ink, it stays comfortable for long reading sessions, even outdoors in bright sunlight.

Battery life is one of the best reasons to own a Kindle, and the Colorsoft can last up to eight weeks between charges. It’s waterproof too, so reading in the bath or by the pool is no problem, and the 16GB of storage holds thousands of books.

This is the standard Kindle Colorsoft rather than the Signature Edition, which adds wireless charging and an auto-adjusting front light. For most readers, the standard model covers everything they need.

With a 4.5-star rating on Amazon from more than 3,000 reviews, the Kindle Colorsoft makes a great gift for a graphic novel fan or anyone ready to move on from an older black-and-white Kindle.

items.body: Apple is facing a formal probe in South Korea over allegations that its iPhone 16 advertising misled consumers about the availability of Apple Intelligence features. Investigators at the country's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) have referred Apple and Apple Korea for review , alleging that several Apple Intelligence features were not delivered as advertised, including Genmoji, Image Playground, and Siri's ability to understand personal context and onscreen awareness. The allegations focus on whether Apple adequately explained which features were available and when others would arrive. For example, the FTC's report notes that Siri's personal-context capabilities were advertised for Korean availability in early April 2025 but did not arrive until October 2026, approximately 18 months later. items.summary: The Motorola Signature 27 is a worthy flagship, but it takes more than top-tier specs to create a winning device.
items.body:

Mobile

Motorola Signature 27 hands-on: A $1,600 flagship that Samsung and Google can't match

The Motorola Signature 27 is a worthy flagship, but it takes more than top-tier specs to create a winning device.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 6:00 AM ET

•

•

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

It’s not a secret that the Motorola Signature 27 was near the top of my list of flagship phones I wanted in 2026. Moto’s been teasing us for years about returning to the US market with a traditional, slab flagship device, and it’s finally a reality. Over the last couple of years, the company has set the table with the well-received Razr lineup. Motorola’s foldables are a sales hit and for good reason.

Now, Motorola hopes that success will extend to the Signature 27. It carries a hefty price tag, but that just seems to be the new reality for smartphones in 2026 and beyond. However, Moto packs plenty for your $1,600. I’ve spent extensive hands-on time with the Signature 27, and here’s why you’ll want one — and why Motorola needs to finish what it started.

Readers' poll

Would you ever consider a Motorola flagship?

4 votes

Motorola nailed the hardware

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

It doesn’t take long to realize the Signature 27 is premium throughout. It feels outstanding in the hand, and I appreciate Motorola’s design choices. The Signature 27 doesn’t so much feature a camera visor or hump as it does a camera plateau. It’s a key design element, and I don’t mind it. The cameras are a highlight of the device, and Motorola made them a cornerstone of the design. I loved it when Xiaomi did that with its 15 Ultra flagship because it gives the phone some flavor — not everything has to be a generic, unoffensive slab.

Under the hood, the Signature 27 plays the part of a flagship phone to perfection. It’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme (Why?) Gen 6 chipset has been snappy in my light testing so far. The phone’s 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage also cement its flagship status. Motorola fitted the Signature 27 with a 6.78-inch tandem AMOLED panel, which it brands as an “Extreme AMOLED Duo” display. While I can’t confirm the display brightness is the full 12,000 nits, even Motorola notes this applies only under certain circumstances and over a small area — your everyday usage will never get near 12,000 nits. However, if you ask me if the display is bright, sharp, and saturated, the answer is yes to all three. In addition, tandem OLED technology should use less power, improving battery life.

Speaking of battery life, I’m particularly excited about the Signature 27’s setup. Google and Samsung have lagged behind their overseas counterparts in bringing larger-capacity silicon-carbon cells to US phones. Motorola counters that with a sizeable 7,000mAh silicon-carbon battery in the Signature 27, with 90W wired charging and 50W wireless charging — easily besting what Samsung and Google currently offer. It should be a highlight of the phone, and I’m glad Motorola included it.

Motorola puts the cameras center stage

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

I mentioned the cameras being a focal point of the Signature 27’s design, and that’s for good reason. The phone’s triple-camera setup is formidable, with a 50MP primary shooter, a 50MP ultrawide lens, and a 200MP 3x periscope zoom lens. I know the 200MP sensor will get plenty of attention, but the 50MP primary camera interests me most. It’s not quite a 1-inch sensor at 1/1.28”, but it’s slightly larger than what you currently get from the competition in the US. A larger sensor means more light and data for the phone to work with when it’s processing images. Paired with the f/1.6 aperture, I expect solid low-light images — and that’s what I’ve seen in my early testing. I was trying to capture a challenging New York City skyline at dusk, and the Signature 27 produced some gorgeous photos.

That’s backed up by the device’s other certifications and awards, including a DXOMARK Gold Label for 2027. Motorola put time and effort into the Signature 27’s camera system, and I can definitely see the results.

Still plenty of question marks for the Signature 27

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

I mentioned earlier that Motorola did the hard part, but now the company has to finish the job. It’s promising 7 years of software support for the Signature 27, which is what we’ve come to expect for flagship phones. Unfortunately, I can’t confidently say what that support will look like. Motorola has a spotty track record, and promised support (even on expensive phones) can sometimes be delayed. I’ve seen encouraging signs with the Motorola Razr Fold, and Android 17 is already running out of the box on the Signature 27, but Moto can’t slip back into old habits when people are paying $1,600.

The price tag is also a concern. In a vacuum, it’s a huge sum, even for an impressive smartphone, but the marketplace doesn’t work that way. If you spec out a Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra with 512GB of storage without any discounts, it’s $1,600. So while the Signature 27’s price is a concern, it’s not that far from what’s currently available — and I’m curious to see what Samsung does with the Galaxy S27 lineup. I can accept and understand something as reality without liking it, and that’s where I land on the Signature 27’s price tag. However, Motorola could do something to help us.

Carrier stores have to play a role in Motorola’s rollout

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Right now, the Signature 27 isn’t available to purchase through carrier stores in the US, which I hope changes soon. Carrier store presence is Motorola’s main advantage over companies like OnePlus and Nothing, which would otherwise compete with Samsung and Google. The sticker shock of $1,600 hits harder for the Signature 27 than for other phones, because I see that number up front. If it were a Pixel 11 Pro XL and I spread the payments out over three years, it wouldn’t hurt as much. Carriers also offer various outsized trade-in offers and discounts that Moto would get access to with the Signature 27.

The sticker shock of $1,600 hits harder for the Signature 27 than for other phones.

It’s how people in the US buy these expensive smartphones, and Motorola needs to leverage that. All told, I think the Signature 27 will be a winner. It’s a legitimate flagship contender, and it’s a phone I’ve been waiting for a long time. However, the spec sheet and hardware aren’t the entire story, and Motorola will need to deliver on the rest.

The Motorola Signature 27 combines premium design, a stunning tandem AMOLED display, flagship performance, and a versatile triple-camera system. Its massive 7,000mAh battery and fast wired and wireless charging make it a compelling flagship contender.

New Play Store requirements force app developers to publish their addresses online

The only way to avoid Google's requirement is to pull your apps from Europe and the UK.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 6:00 AM ET

•

•

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google is reportedly facing privacy concerns over a requirement for app developers to disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses.

• The requirement applies to all app developers, including solo creators, who offer their apps in Europe and the UK.

• The company won’t allow developers to use a PO box, leading at least one creator to say they might rent a separate office.

Google and partners started rolling out developer verification for Android apps earlier this year, along with a more convoluted sideloading process on devices. These new measures will launch globally in January, but another Google requirement is under scrutiny due to privacy issues.

The Elec reports that Google is facing privacy concerns over a recent requirement that app developers (including solo creators) publicly disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses on Google Play. This move, which kicks in from March 2027, is meant to help Google and developers comply with European regulatory requirements. However, the outlet adds that developer addresses and phone numbers will be shown worldwide.

Readers' poll

Do you think app developers should publicly list their address on Google Play?

13 votes

“I don’t need a separate office to develop and operate games, but I’m considering renting one to protect my personal information,” an independent developer was quoted as saying by The Elec. “Disclosing developers’ home addresses amounts to an invasion of privacy.”

A step too far for individual developers?

These requirements are related to Google’s trade status declaration process. The company explained in a support page last month that “all active developer accounts” distributing apps in Europe or the UK need to declare whether they are a trader or non-trader by February 1, 2027. Google notes that developers should declare themselves as traders if they have ad-supported apps, paid apps, or apps with in-app purchases. Those who declare themselves as traders will have their address and phone number publicly displayed. However, the search giant clarifies that developers who don’t offer their apps in Europe or the UK can declare themselves a non-trader, presumably avoiding the public address and phone number requirement.

Google also explicitly notes in its support page that phone numbers and addresses of personal developer accounts will be publicly shown:

If you use a personal developer account, you must provide a contact phone number to be displayed on Google Play. Be aware that your address will also be publicly displayed.

An Australian developer used Google’s support forum to complain about these disclosure requirements:

I’m a solo developer in Australia with a personal account and one small app (a single paying subscriber). To comply with the trader declaration, I’d have to publish my home address and phone number to users worldwide from March 2027. Support confirmed PO Boxes aren’t accepted, since the address must match my verified residential address.
The law behind this (EU DSA / UK DMCCA) only requires disclosure to EEA and UK consumers, yet Google is choosing to display these details globally. My only privacy-safe option is to withdraw my app from 31 countries and declare as a non-trader.

“Publishing a home address is a real safety risk for solo developers, especially those working from home,” the Australian developer added. “I’d love to stay available in the EU and UK, but not at the cost of my personal safety.”

Developers have also taken to Reddit to criticize the publication of addresses, with one user claiming that Google was “backing developers into a corner.” Another user warned that bad actors could scrape Google Play to get every developer’s address and phone number.

In any event, we’ve asked Google for comment regarding this matter and whether it’ll allow PO boxes in response to privacy concerns. We’ll update the article as soon as the company gets back to us. I can certainly understand displaying a phone number as an alternative to email support, but forcing individual developers to publicly share their physical address seems like a step too far.

Here are the best T-Mobile T-Mix perks to choose (and what to avoid)

Not every T-Mix perk is worth it, but there are a few that stand above the rest.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 5:00 AM ET

•

•

T-Mobile

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

The new T-Mix plans are here, though we’ve already concluded that for most users there are probably better options out there. For those who aren’t aware, the new T-Mix plans drop extras like free T-Satellite access, streaming services, or even special free phone deals. Instead, each plan gives you a certain amount of points that you can use in combination to pick streaming services, phone offers, and more.

If you absolutely have your heart set on a T-Mix plan, you’ll at least want to make the best of the perks available. Let’s jump in and look at the best perks available, as well as ones you might want to avoid.

What are the best perks available on T-Mix?

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

One of the most important things to know is that not all T-Mobile T-Mix perks are of equal value. Some perks cost multiple “pick” points, and even within similar categories, the actual retail value can vary wildly. From a purely cost-value perspective, the three best perks are Apple TV ($14.99/month), Hulu with Ads ($12.49/month), and SiriusXM All Access ($11.99/month). Just keep in mind that Apple TV’s one-pick price is a limited-time deal: it costs one pick through June 2027, then jumps to two picks.

Of course, what apps and services you use comes down to personal preferences. While the three above are a good deal because they only cost one pick each and have values above $10, here are some of the other solid options for 1-pick perks:

• Paramount Plus Essential – $8.99

• Netflix Standard with Ads – $8.99

• YouTube Premium Lite – $8.99

• DashPass by DoorDash – $9.99

• Google AI Plus 2TB – $9.99

• T-Sat – $10

Beyond the 1-pick offers, the value gets a little less impressive if I’m honest. Most 2-pick offers range in value from $11.99 to $19.99, with only a few like Google AI Pro ($19.99 monthly value) really worth it. The same applies to the few 3- and 4-pick perks, which range from $19.99 to $31.99 in monthly value.

Generally speaking, the best deals are for movie and TV streaming. Music streaming perks tend to cost a lot more points, though SiriusXM is a rare exception. It’s also worth noting this only gives you app access, so there’s no built-in car sat radio support with this plan.

In addition to streaming perks and other subscription services, you can also use your picks to activate phone deals. The actual value of these options ranges dramatically and can take anywhere from one to four pick points. Don’t assume all low-point offers are low value, either. For example, both the Moto G (2026) and Moto Razr cost a single pick point, despite the latter being a much more expensive device.

Which perks are best avoided?

Taylor Kerns / Android Authority

Above, we talked about some of the perks that we feel are worth it, but are there any that are worth avoiding? For my vote, I’d say Delta Air Lines points and Pandora Plus are at the top of the list. Both use one pick each and have values right around $5-6, which means you’re better saying your perk points for something else.

Honestly, the same goes for Apple Music Individual ($11.99 monthly value) and Pandora Premium ($11.99 monthly value). These both use two pick points each and yet have values similar to many of the better one-pick choices like Apple TV.

Are these T-Mix plans even worth it for the Picks/Perks?

T-Mobile

Keep in mind this is far from a comprehensive look at every perk, and there could certainly be a few others worth looking at.

Maybe you aren’t into movies and TV and prefer to use up three points on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate ($22.99) or use four picks on ESPN Unlimited ($31.99). These might not be great in the cost-to-value department on paper, but if you aren’t going to use the others and have points left to spend? Why not.

The biggest thing to remember is that in nearly every case the combined value of plan features and perks will still be more expensive than if you went with a prepaid plan or stuck with a better legacy postpaid plan. For those who aren’t already on a legacy plan and are unwilling to give prepaid a try, it could still be worth it; just don’t go in expecting to get a great value here.

Three wake words, one surprisingly close reader poll.

For what feels like decades, “OK Google” activated the company’s various smart home, voice assistant, and audio-triggered features. Then came “Hey Google,” and the two lived in harmony for several years. However, there’s a new wake word that Google wants to sear into your memory. Starting with Intelligent Eyewear, “Hey Gemini” will be the preferred trigger word for Android XR. While the old phrase will still work, Google is actively guiding users to involve its newer voice assistant when summoning your digital pal.

Naturally, adapting what has now become muscle memory will be difficult for many, many users — me included. We asked readers what their preferred Google wake word is in a recent survey, and here are the results:
Poll results
What's your Google wake word of choice?
41.1%Hey Google
2,144 votes · androidauthority.com · results as of November 26, 2026

With 41.1% of the vote, “Hey Google” is our readers’ preferred way to trigger Google’s audio assistant and features. Surprisingly, 30% of readers side with “Hey Gemini,” while 28.9% use the older “OK Google” hotword.
That’s a surprisingly even spread across the three options available and suggests that users prefer having a choice rather than being prescribed a way to use their devices.
For some, “Hey Google” just rolls off the tongue. Memory certainly plays a role for users who prefer this option, too.

The Blurams F20C solar camera sees what my video doorbell misses

This outdoor security camera was able to solve my problem.

Brought to you by Blurams

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 4:22 AM ET

•

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

My doorbell camera works great at showing who’s at my front door. However, it leaves me with a couple of blind spots. First, it doesn’t show my package at the bottom of the door when it’s delivered. If I’m not home, that package might sit there for hours, making it vulnerable to theft by a porch pirate. My low-tech solution was to put a sign under the door asking the driver to place the package into a box next to my door. However, this creates a second blind spot because my doorbell camera doesn’t show packages going into the box.

With the Blurams F20C 4K Solar Outdoor Security Camera, my goal was to eliminate these two blind spots. I mounted it to a tree that faces my front door so I can see if the driver leaves the package at the front door or if they put it into the delivery box. So, is a solar-powered camera with no wires reliable enough to keep watch over my deliveries all day?

Why a doorbell camera isn’t the best solution to track package deliveries

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

A lot of people buy a doorbell camera to track their online deliveries. In my experience, they leave out a lot. Not only do they have a fixed angle that’s usually pointed at face height, but they also tend to record short clips only after motion triggers them. This problem arises because traditional motion-triggered cameras use a PIR sensor. This means that they wake up when movement is detected. In theory, this sounds smart, but in reality, I noticed that most clips start late and end early, leaving homeowners like me both frustrated and anxious.

The F20C takes a different approach, which I’ll explain later in more detail. Let’s start with the basics first.

What’s in the box

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

Inside the box, you’ll find the 4K Ultra HD camera, a solar panel, mounting hardware, and screw packs.

The F20C has a 5W solar panel, a large 12,000mAh battery, and it supports local storage on a microSD card up to 512GB. That means you’re not forced into a monthly cloud plan to store and watch your footage, like with some of its competitors. Extended cloud storage is optional, with free single-day cloud storage also available. It has an IP66 waterproof rating, making it rain, snow, and dust resistant, so you can leave it out without a problem. It supports both 2.4GHz and 5GHz WiFi 6 connections for outdoor monitoring.

Setup is very DIY friendly

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

After downloading the Blurams app, setup took only about 5 minutes. You simply pick the F20C from the selection of Blurams cameras and follow the app instructions to connect it to the app.

The physical install is where things got interesting. At first, I installed it on a wooden post facing my front door. I installed the mounting bracket with two screws and slid the camera into the slot. Later, I decided to mount it on a tree closer to my front door instead. This gave me a much better viewing angle of my front gate, the walkway, and front door with the 360° Pan and 90° tilt feature.

The F20C supports two solar setups. The panel can attach directly to the camera to make it a single unit. Alternatively, if there is a better area that gets more sunlight, the solar panel can be detached and mounted in a separate location. The panel has a long 3-meter USB-C cable to enable this. For aesthetic reasons, I mounted it as a single unit, but if I were running out of power, I was prepared to move the solar panel to the other side of the tree. So far, it’s worked perfectly as a single unit, but things may change as we get into the shorter days of winter.

It comes with a free trial for cloud storage

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The F20C comes with a free one-month trial of Blurams’ Basic cloud plan for one camera. It stores either seven days of 24/7 continuous recording or 15 days of motion-triggered clips. The plan also includes Smart Detection, which can tell the difference between people, vehicles, and packages, so you get fewer false alarms. While package detection is part of the paid cloud service, a free on-device package detection will be introduced in a future update. This will filter package-related events without requiring a subscription. You also get rich notifications, which show a snapshot right on your lock screen.

Once the trial ends, you still get some free cloud features. This includes motion and sound alerts, event snapshots, and 12-second event recordings that are stored for one day. That’s not much, so I installed a microSD card to record footage locally. If you don’t want to pay for a monthly cloud plan, I recommend doing the same.

AOV vs PIR: No missing moments

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

AOV stands for Always-on Video, and it’s Blurams’ low-power continuous recording approach. Instead of sleeping until the motion sensor wakes it, the camera stays in a low-power state and records the entire time. PIR (passive infrared) cameras only wake up when they detect a change in infrared heat, which is why their clips often miss the start. With AOV, there’s no gap at the beginning of a clip, and nothing cut off at the end. Having now tried both types of cameras, I definitely prefer AOV cameras because they provide a full video timeline.

What it caught at my front door

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

This is the part I cared about most. Before the F20C, I already knew packages were arriving because of the alerts my doorbell camera provided. But the doorbell clips were never perfect. They either started too late, after the driver had already reached the door, or cut out too early.

Now, I can see the whole sequence. With the Smart AI detection, Always-on Video (AOV), and pan/tilt/zoom (PTZ), I saw the delivery driver open the front gate, walk to the door, read the sign on the bottom, and place the package into the box. This is the peace of mind I was hoping to get from my video doorbell. With the F20C, all the blind spots were eliminated.

To date, I haven’t had a single package stolen. But the F20C did capture something I wasn’t expecting. One evening, while I was working in my home office, I got a notification from both my video doorbell camera and the Blurams F20C. I looked at the footage on my doorbell camera and saw someone walk up to my door. Unfortunately, the doorbell camera stopped recording once they got to the door. I immediately opened the Blurams app and watched that footage. This person was walking down the sidewalk, saw the sign under the door, and mistook it for a package. As soon as he got to the door, he realized it was just a sign. He turned around and left empty-handed.

To reiterate, my doorbell camera only saw him arrive. The F20C saw what he was looking at, and showed him walking away afterwards. I saw the entire sequence in a single video clip. That’s the kind of context a single doorbell camera angle can’t give you. Right then and there, it convinced me that a backup camera on the front door was a great idea.

Video quality, day and night

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The F20C records up to 4K Ultra HD at 2160p resolution, but users can adjust it to Full High Definition (FHD) at 1296p, or High Definition (HD) at 720p. Higher video quality requires more internet bandwidth, so I keep it at FHD to be safe.

Users have several options for night vision to choose from. This is something I haven’t seen in other security cameras. IR Night Vision provides night vision mode in black and white. This is the ideal setting for viewing longer distances. Intelligent Night Vision provides a black and white image when no motion is detected. However, when motion is detected, the video automatically shifts into full color mode. Another option is Color Night Vision, which turns on the white light when the F20C enters night vision mode. Finally, Forced Night Vision enables black and white night vision mode without being affected by the light environment.

I set the F20C to Intelligent Night Vision, which I feel is the best all-around setting for most users. In this setting, the white light will turn off with a delay after the motion stops.

Smart alerts to prevent notification overload

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The last thing anyone wants from an outdoor security camera is unnecessary notifications. The F20C uses on-device AI to recognize humans, pets, vehicles, and packages through a paid cloud service plan. A future update will soon provide on-device AI package detection for free. This provides context to any notification alerts. Users can also set a schedule for receiving notifications. Since I’m using this to track package deliveries, I’m keeping the F20C armed with Human Detection enabled so it only starts recording when a human event is detected. If my neighbor’s cat comes into frame, I will not receive a notification.

There’s also a dedicated Package Detection alert notification that will soon be free after a future update. With a paid cloud subscription, users can also enable rich notification alerts for packages. I’m considering a paid cloud subscription for rich notifications since tracking packages is the primary reason I’ve installed the F20C.

Users can also enable a Perimeter Alarm and specify the alert period. I set the alarm to turn on between 10pm and 4am for any Human detection during the night. If someone comes into my front yard during the night, a sound alert will go on 5 times along with a flashing light alert for 10 seconds. This acts as a deterrent for any thief trying to break into my house.

Should you buy the Blurams F20C?

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The whole point of reviewing this camera was to see if it can solve a specific problem I have with package deliveries. Did the delivery driver place it on the ground, or follow my instructions to place it in the box beside my door? The F20C solved it. To my surprise, it also caught someone looking for a package that wasn’t there.

The Blurams F20C is a good fit for homeowners who want to store and review footage without paying a subscription plan. You get a lot of peace of mind with this product. It’s DIY friendly because you don’t have to fiddle around with wires or connect it to a power source. With solar charging, it can be placed virtually anywhere without worrying about charging it again. What impressed me the most is how it records the whole event instead of fragmented clips that start too late or end too early. That alone makes this camera easy to recommend.

My advice is to take advantage of the Black Friday deals. The F20C is currently available for $65.99, down from $149.99. You can also get two of them for $121.99. The company also has deals available on its cloud storage plans, if you’re interested in them. The promotion period runs from November 19 to November 30th.

After Black Friday and Cyber Monday, Android Authority readers can still get these exclusive savings on Amazon from November 19 to December 31. Use Discount Code: AAUSFC1P for the 1-Pack and AAUSFC2P for the 2-Pack.

If you’ve been thinking about getting a home security camera, take advantage of these Black Friday deals for the F20C and the cloud storage. There’s peace of mind knowing you’ll have footage of any event that matters to you.
